stage1.impression: A crisp, legible macro of a Hypex plate set into a glowing orange acrylic body; the graphics and connectors read well and the tinted glass has real depth. But every surface is CG-clean (the plate is a flat, evenly lit grey card with no grain, no dust, no light falling across it), the orange glow is saturated to the point of looking emissive, and the bottom fifth is an empty orange block. It reads as an excellent product visualisation, not a photograph.

blocking_9: The amp plate must carry a visible light gradient and surface texture (panel interior lum_range >= 22, falloff along y), not read as a flat printed card
The frame needs an exposure and air that belong beside a high-key white hero (whole-frame lum median nearer 100 than 79), without clipping the acrylic edge glows
The acrylic edge glows must not saturate the red channel (R 251 at x 420-470)
The composition must give the plate and rating plate a clear hierarchy, with no empty orange block taking the bottom 20 percent of the frame
The finish must show some evidence of a real object (fine bead-blast on the plate, a trace of dust on the horizontal ledges), since nothing in the frame now has micro-detail

defects.what: Amp plate evenly lit, lum_range 16.3 (p5 75, p95 91): no falloff, no texture, reads as a decal on a card
Left acrylic edge glow at r_median 251, g 100: red channel at clip, reads as a neon tube rather than light in a polished edge
Top strip saturated orange (R128 G44 B17) with 0.14 percent clipping; a bright red-orange band crowds the top edge
Large featureless orange block below the plate (lum 70-116, no detail), dead space that pulls the eye down
Rating plate looks pasted onto the acrylic: same flat matte grey, no contact or reflection, very small text
No dust, fingerprints or bead-blast anywhere despite the shot's name; every surface is CG-clean
Panel frame bevel is a soft 68 px ramp with no crisp specular line on the machined edge

changes.problem: The amp plate is lit flat and frontally, so it reads as a printed card rather than a machined, anodised plate.

evidence.measured: lum_median 80.1, p5 75.2, p95 91.5, range 16.3: almost no gradient across 400 px of plate

change.to: azimuth_deg -70, elevation_deg 62, distance_m 3.0 (raking from upper side across the plate), size_m 1.2 -> 0.8

changes.expected: A soft top-to-bottom and side-to-side falloff across the plate, with screw heads and connector rims throwing short shadows; the plate's top third about 20 percent brighter than its bottom third.

changes.problem: Nothing in the frame has micro-detail; the shot is named for dust but none shows, and the plate has no anodised grain.

evidence.measured: Crops at 2x show perfectly uniform grey between graphics; no grain or particles visible anywhere

change.setting: finish / plate material (set dressing, not geometry)
change.from: uniform matte grey, no surface noise
change.to: fine bead-blast bump on the plate (noise scale ~0.2 mm, strength 0.05, roughness varying 0.45-0.6) and a sparse dust layer on upward-facing ledges (frame bottom lip, ledge below the plate): particle density low, 0.05-0.2 mm, caught by the raking key

changes.expected: Under the raking key the plate shows a fine satin grain and a few specks on the lower lip of the recess; the plate stops reading as a decal.

changes.problem: The polished acrylic edges glow at red-channel clip and read as neon tubes.
changes.expected: The edge glows stay the brightest orange in the frame but keep tonal gradation along their length; the red channel stays below clip.

changes.problem: The bottom fifth of the frame is an empty orange block, and the rating plate, the second subject, is pushed to the left edge.

evidence.measured: Featureless area, lum 70-116, about 13 percent of the frame with no detail

change.to: target z 0.535 and x 0.075 (raise and shift the frame so the plate's bottom edge sits at about 88 percent of frame height and the rating plate moves to about 30 percent from the left), lens 85 -> 100

changes.expected: The plate fills the frame top to bottom with even margins, the rating plate sits on a third line, and the empty block leaves the frame.

changes.problem: The frame is dim for a detail meant to sit beside a high-key white hero.

change.to: +0.35 (after c3, so edges do not clip)

changes.expected: The orange body reads as lit, translucent acrylic rather than a dim glow, and the plate's greys move from 80 to about 95.

changes.problem: The plate's machined bevel has no crisp specular line, so its edges look soft and modelled.

change.to: orbit azimuth 35, elevation 30, strength 6.0 (move the strip to the camera's other side so it draws a thin highlight down the right bevel of the recess)

changes.expected: A thin bright line along the recess's right bevel and the plate's edge, 3-6 px wide.

changes.problem: A saturated red-orange band along the top edge pulls the eye out of the frame.

change.to: a soft top and bottom graduated burn of -0.3 EV over the outer 10 percent of the frame

changes.expected: Edges quieter than the plate; the eye settles on the connectors and wordmark.

changes.problem: The rating plate is lit identically to the amp plate and looks pasted on, with tiny text.

evidence.measured: lum_median 72.5, same neutral grey as the amp plate (R73 G72 B76)

change.to: 2.4, with the target moved to [0.0, 0.0, 0.55] so the scrim's soft reflection falls across the rating plate

changes.expected: The rating plate picks up a soft sheen that separates it from the acrylic, a touch brighter than the amp plate.

out_of_scope.request: Reduce the saturation of the orange acrylic tint
out_of_scope.why: The colour is the speaker's own and is fixed; only the light on it may change (c3, c5).
The rating plate is a part of the speaker.
